_comment: Editor UI metadata for MPC B-LEG. Overlaid onto the schema built from BLegConfig (a SosFadeConfig superset). UI ONLY — never touches a trade decision or the source hash. Click Scan Strategies after editing. Params not listed here fall back to their raw field names; the A+ gate params (arm sources, FVG/entry, HTF, veto) are inherited from the A+ bot and still matter because the B-LEG keeps the 'A+ has priority' stand-down — see the A+ strategy's own meta for their descriptions. Labels and descs are shared with indicators/mpc_b_leg_strategy.pine the same way the A+ meta is — label == the Pine input title, desc == its tooltip, changed in the same commit. COPY STYLE (2026-08-10, Aaron's call): every desc is SHORT and PLAIN — what the setting does, what each choice means, and the one fact that changes the decision. No measurement dumps, no trade counts, no R figures, no dates, no file references: the strategy detail page is for reading, and the evidence behind a default lives in this package's CLAUDE.md and its optimization doc. Same rule for `edge` and `steps`.
edge: This is the reversal whose pullback turned up late. Structure breaks, but instead of pulling back the market runs on, so the normal setup dies with no trade at all. This one remembers the level and leaves an order there for a few days in case price comes back. Often it does. Everything after the entry is handled the same way as the main bot.

steps.label: 01 · Break
steps.title: A reversal fires
steps.detail: Structure breaks and the level to watch is marked, even though the reversal itself has not traded yet.

steps.label: 02 · Runs on
steps.title: The pullback never comes
steps.detail: Price expands and breaks structure again before pulling back, so the normal reversal dies with no trade. That death is what starts this setup.

steps.label: 03 · Late
steps.title: The pullback arrives anyway
steps.detail: An order rests at the marked level for a few days. If price comes back to it, the order fills. If it never comes back, or runs too far the other way, the setup is dropped.

steps.label: 04 · Manage
steps.title: Let it run
steps.detail: The same machinery as the main bot: the first target moves the stop to breakeven, the second lifts it further, and the trailing stop takes the rest.

params.name: bleg_max_days
params.label: Days to watch for the late retrace
params.desc: How long the order waits at the frozen level for the late pullback before the setup is dropped. Set in days but counted in bars, so weekends and the daily close do not use it up. Lower means only quick pullbacks fill; four to five days tested best.
guide: Waits longer for a late return — 4 to 5 days tested best

params.name: exec_risk_pct
params.label: Risk % per trade
params.desc: How much of the account each trade risks. Position size is worked back from this and the stop distance, so a tighter stop buys a bigger position at the same risk.

params.name: exec_longs
params.label: Trade longs
params.desc: On = long setups may trade. Off = shorts only.

params.name: exec_shorts
params.label: Trade shorts
params.desc: On = short setups may trade. Off = longs only.

params.name: exec_no_late_day
params.label: No entries in the final hour (16:00-17:00 NY)
params.desc: On = no new entries in the last hour before the daily close. Gold closes at 17:00 New York and reopens at 18:00, so a trade opened late can be gapped out over the break.

params.name: exec_runner_trail
params.label: Runner trail method
params.desc: How the stop follows the trade once the second target is hit, and which setting below is live. Fixed step is a plain dollar grid. Structure parks the stop at the last swing, which breathes with the trend but hands a lot back at the turn. Structure + ratchet is the default and banks more of each run.
guide: Fixed step — simplest, and the worst of the three
Structure + ratchet — best on the main bot, untested here

params.name: exec_struct_trail_buf_tk
params.label: Structure trail buffer (ticks)
params.desc: Used by both structure methods. The trailing stop sits this many ticks beyond the last swing, so a wick through it does not clip you.
guide: Tight to the swing — clipped by wicks
Wide of the swing — survives noise, gives back more

params.name: exec_trail_pct
params.label: Runner ratchet step (% of price)
params.desc: How big each step of the trailing stop is, as a percent of price. It has to be far smaller here than on the main bot: these trades risk very little of the price, so a big step is bigger than the whole trade and the stop never moves at all.
guide: Tighter — banks more of each run on this setup
Too big and the stop never moves at all here

params.name: exec_trail_step
params.label: Runner trail step ($ of price)
params.desc: The step size in dollars. Read by two settings, so it is never greyed out: the fixed-step trail, and the one-step-behind stop floor. On gold 1 pip is 10 cents, so 50 pips = 5.0.
guide: Tighter trail — banks sooner, cuts runners short
Looser trail — lets winners breathe, gives back more

params.name: exec_tp2_stop_mode
params.label: TP2 → stop floor
params.desc: Where the stop jumps to the moment the second target is hit, before the trail takes over. TP1 price is tight and can scratch the trade on the first pullback. Breakeven gives it the most room. One trail step behind keeps it just under the best price seen. The trail can still tighten past this.
guide: TP1 price — protects the gain, scratches runners
Breakeven — maximum room for the runner

params.name: exec_time_stop_mode
params.label: Time stop
params.desc: Close a trade that has been open longer than the hours set below. Before TP1 only fires while the trade has never reached the first target, so it cuts no winners. Always closes on the clock alone. Off closes nothing, and on this setup that tested worst.
guide: Off — the clock never closes a trade
Always — the clock closes winners too

params.name: exec_time_stop_hrs
params.label: Time stop (hours)
params.desc: How long a trade may stay open, in hours, weekends included. Anything from about 4 to 12 hours gives the same answer here. What it buys is a smaller drawdown rather than more profit.
guide: Cuts winners as well as losers

params.name: exec_aplus
params.label: A+ has priority (stand the B-leg down)

options.on: A+ stands the B leg down

params.desc: In this bot the main reversal setup never places an order — it only holds first claim. On = on a side where the main setup would have armed, this one stands down, which keeps results comparable with the parent. Off = every setup here trades on its own merit.
